--- Summary (auto) ---
Redwood walked through region pinning options and guarantees, KMS model (BYOK vs Redwood-managed keys), audit log retention, and sub-processor disclosure. Finovate reiterated requirement for EU-only processing for PII workloads and asked about fallback behavior, cross-border telemetry, and contractual language.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time, we'll do a quick security review focused on data residency and region pinning. Liam from the SE team will cover the architecture.
[00:18] Sara (Finovate): Great, thanks. To start: our legal/compliance folks say any PII must be processed and stored in the EU. We need strong guarantees and proof of sub-processors.
[00:28] Liam (SE): Yep understood. We'll show our region pinning model. At a high level, customers can opt for EU-only routing — requests and storage stay in region; if capacity isn't available we can fail closed or route to a dedicated EU capacity pool. There are a couple of modes, we can go over them.
[00:45] Mark (CTO): Is that for hosted only or also dedicated/private? We have some teams that want private deployment but prefer cloud first.
[00:52] Liam (SE): Good question. Region pinning works across Hosted and Dedicated. For Private (VPC/on-prem) you'd be controlling the infra so it's naturally EU. For Hosted we provide logical routing and physical placement — we keep datasets and KV caches in the chosen region. Small note: some telemetry (health metrics, anonymized) may cross border unless you opt-out via enterprise plan.
[01:15] Elena (Sec): Can you be explicit about telemetry? Our compliance team flags any metadata leaving the EU.
[01:22] Maya (AE): Yes, we have an enterprise setting to disable cross-border telemetry; we'll include that in the doc. But we need to be explicit about subprocessors like cloud providers and monitoring vendors.
[01:34] Sara: Also how do keys work — we want to use our own KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest with strict key control.
[01:42] Liam: We support two models: Redwood-managed keys (encryption-at-rest, keys in region) or customer-managed keys (BYOK) with KMS integration. For highest control you can use your KMS via a cross-account key grant; AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault supported, HSM via partner integrations. Note: when using BYOK, we never persist key material on our side.
[02:05] Mark: If we do BYOK and EU-pin, does any data get replicated to the US for model caching or KV caches?
[02:13] Liam: No for pinned tenants we don't replicate persistent data cross-region. We do have ephemeral model cache shards that can be in region; historically some internal logs used a global aggregator and that was the friction point. We've changed it: aggregator can be configured per-tenant to process only in region, or disabled.
[02:33] Sara: Are the audit logs exportable? Our auditors want a copy in our SIEM and retention 7 years.
[02:40] Liam: Yes, audit logs are available via an S3 export to a customer-owned bucket in the chosen region, and we can do streaming to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. Retention is configurable — default 90 days but enterprise customers can request longer retention. We'll surface retention SLA and e-discovery options.
[02:58] Elena: On the sub-processor list — is that static? We need the full list and any planned changes with 30-day notice. Also which sub-processors have access to PII?
[03:06] Maya: We publish an up-to-date sub-processor list and provide notification of changes. Access to PII is restricted; only infra providers for compute/storage have potential access and are covered by contract. We'll send the document and the legal team can review any addenda.
[03:20] Speaker 1 (auto): (audio glitch) uh-huh, sorry overlapped, go on.
[03:26] Mark: How about SLA if EU capacity is saturated? Do you fail the request, queue it, or route to US? We can't allow inadvertent cross-border processing.
[03:36] Liam: We support three behaviors configurable per-tenant or per-route: fail-fast (return capacity error), queue-within-region (longer latency), or route-to-dedicated-licensed EU pool (additional cost). We do not default to US routing for pinned tenants.
[03:53] Sara: Good. Can you quantify latencies if we pick queue vs dedicated? We need numbers for our SRE to model.
[04:01] Liam: Rough guidance: queue adds variable delay (hundreds ms up to seconds depending on backlog); dedicated EU pool gives predictable p95 within our published benchmarks — I'll attach a benchmark sheet with EU region numbers. Note that model choice and sequence length matter.
[04:22] Elena: On SSO/RBAC: we want SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning and role-based access that maps to our internal roles.
[04:31] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is configurable and you can map to groups. We also have audit trails for token-level usage.
[04:42] Sara: One more: contractually we need explicit warranty that PII remains in EU except for legal process or with consent. Is that standard?
[04:50] Maya: We can include contractual language in the DPA to state processing remains in EU for pinned workloads and describe lawful transfer exceptions. Legal will provide standard addenda — we can share a draft.
[05:02] Mark: Any dependencies on third parties that might process cross-border? e.g., analytics vendors?
[05:08] Liam: We use a small set of monitoring and error-reporting vendors. For enterprise EU-pin customers we can either stop sending telemetry to global vendors or route telemetry to EU-only sub-processors. We'll include the list and options.
[05:21] Elena: Regarding KMS: we need assurance keys are not exportable and that Redwood personnel cannot decrypt data without a legal process.
[05:29] Liam: For BYOK with customer-managed keys, Redwood never has access to key material; operations can't decrypt without the key. For Redwood-managed keys we use KMS and HSM-backed stores; access is strictly role-gated and logged. We also support HSM-backed keys via partners if you need FIPS/HSM attestation.
[05:49] Sara: What about logs for all admin actions — immutable audit? We need proof for SOC2.
[05:56] Maya: We maintain immutable admin audit logs with cryptographic integrity options for enterprise — that's in the SOC2 scope. We'll send the SOC2 attestation and details.
[06:05] Elena: Cross-border backups? Some providers snapshot to a multi-region bucket for DR.
[06:12] Liam: For pinned tenants we can keep backups in-region; our DR playbook allows cross-region DR only with consent. There is an option for geo-redundant backups within the EU (multi-az) but not cross-continent unless you opt-in.
[06:29] Sara: If we need to prove residency, can you provide per-request headers showing region handling?
[06:36] Liam: Yes — we can add X-Redwood-Region headers and include region in audit logs and exports.
[06:43] Speaker 2 (auto): (brief crosstalk)
[06:46] Maya: Quick note on sub-processors: we'll include the sub-processor attestation and data access controls in the packet. Also, our default SLA for notifications of changes is 30 days.
[06:58] Mark: On encryption in transit — TLS is standard but what about mutual TLS for service-to-service?
[07:04] Liam: We support mTLS for dedicated/private deployments and can enable it for hosted customer endpoints upon request. Standard TLS with strict ciphers is enabled by default.
[07:18] Sara: Do you have a runbook for cross-border incident response? If an incident potentially exposes data that moved cross-border, we need to know timelines and notification thresholds.
[07:29] Maya: Yes, incident response timelines are in the DPA: 72 hours for major incidents plus ongoing updates. For cross-border exposures we provide details per incident and can support forensic packages.
[07:40] Elena: About sub-processors again — who manages data subject requests? If an EU citizen submits a DSAR, what's the flow?
[07:48] Liam: We assist customers with DSARs; in pinned setups the data controller (customer) retains obligations, Redwood is a processor and can export records to help fulfill DSARs. We can support exports in standard formats.
[07:59] Sara: Anything else we should know?
[08:03] Liam: One operational caveat: if you want both EU pinning and very low cost, certain batching and caching optimizations we recommend are global; to keep everything EU-only some micro-optimizations may be disabled — small cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[08:21] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send SOC2/ISO bundle and sub-processor list, Liam will share region pinning design and topology, and Elena will send compliance checklist. We should schedule a deep technical review next week.
[08:36] Sara: Fine with that, thanks.
[08:39] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
